# Psalm 21 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Translator:** SOPHIA (Council Arbiter) | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** For the choirmaster. A psalm of David.

**2** O LORD, in Your strength the king rejoices, and in Your salvation how greatly he exults!

**3** You have given him his heart's desire and have not withheld the request of his lips. Selah.

**4** For You meet him with rich blessings; You set a crown of fine gold upon his head.

**5** He asked life of You; You gave it to him — length of days forever and ever.

**6** His glory is great through Your salvation; splendor and majesty You bestow on him.

**7** For You make him most blessed forever; You make him glad with the joy of Your presence.

**8** For the king trusts in the LORD, and through the steadfast love of the Most High he shall not be moved.

**9** Your hand will find out all your enemies; your right hand will find out those who hate you.

**10** You will make them as a blazing oven when you appear. The LORD will swallow them up in His wrath, and fire will consume them.

**11** You will destroy their descendants from the earth, and their offspring from among the children of man.

**12** Though they plan evil against you, though they devise schemes, they will not succeed.

**13** For you will put them to flight; you will aim at their faces with your bows.

---
## Council Notes

SOPHIA detected **6** significant divergence(s) in Psalm 21.

- **21:1** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **21:10** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **21:11** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **21:7** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **21:9** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **21:13** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

## Translation Notes (Select)

### EMET
- **21:5**: 'Length of days forever and ever' — the royal hyperbole of the Davidic covenant, pointing beyond any single king's lifetime.

### LOGOS
- **21:8**: The psalm's theological center: the king's stability rests not on military power but on trust in the LORD and His steadfast love.

### PNEUMA
- **21:1-7**: This is the companion to Psalm 20. Psalm 20 is the pre-battle prayer; Psalm 21 is the post-victory celebration. Together they frame the battle.

— SOPHIA
